rv.q: There’s nothing retro and everything urgent about Porchlight Music Theatre’s exquisitely cast, visually stunning production, running through Feb. 12 at the Ruth Page Center for the Arts.
It's clear this CABARET belongs to Stephan's Sally.
Porchlight’s CABARET is truly a unique and memorable experience!

The engine of this “Cabaret” only continues to gain propulsion as each new relationship is forged or broken or as each dream is won or lost, relentlessly pushing the plot and the lives of those involved to go faster and faster.
And Porchlight Music Theatre’s knockout revival of the show is an absolute stunner.

Cue Porchlight Music Theatre’s production of Cabaret, delicately juggling a tale of victims, survivors, and witnesses, capturing magic in the melancholy through bold direction, outstanding choreography, and a jaw-droppingly talented cast.
Who knew that this 1960s musical, based on a 1950s play and a 1939 novel would feel so painfully real in 2023. America.
Porchlight's production of Cabaret is masterfully well-paced so that we can feel the slow descent into fascism.
The entire cast made this production an exhilarating and enthralling musical theatre performance at Porchlight.
This production is every bit as good as the Broadway revivals that too often rely on stunt casting.
Porchlight’s new version of Cabaret will stay with you long after you have left the theater.
Porchlight Music Theatre's "Cabaret" is an outstanding piece of work.

cn.t: Porchlight's production of Cabaret earns widespread acclaim for its timely resonance and polished execution. Critics particularly praise Erica Stephan's captivating Sally Bowles and Michael Weber's insightful direction.
